s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute pulmonary syndrome in an immunocompromised patient with a history of renal transplant
salient_findings: Bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates on chest radiograph
Bilateral diffuse ground-glass opacities on high-resolution CT of the chest
Positive Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain of BAL fluid
New left upper-zone infiltrates after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
Leukopenia with a total lymphocyte count of 1400/μL and ANC of 1050/μL
key_facts: 36-year-old man with end-stage renal disease secondary to IgA nephropathy
Underwent live-related renal transplant 6 months ago
Maintained on tacrolimus 3.5 mg daily, mycophenolate sodium 720 mg daily, and prednisolone 7.5 mg daily
Presented with a 14-day history of low-grade fever, dry cough, and anorexia
Afebrile on admission with heart rate 88 beats/min, blood pressure 122/76 mm Hg, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Bilateral inspiratory crackles on examination
Hemoglobin 14.6 g/dL, total lymphocyte count 9900/μL, absolute neutrophil count 7720/μL, platelets 285 000/μL, serum creatinine 1.05 mg/dL
Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated PaO₂ 68 mm Hg and an A–a gradient of 22 mm Hg
HIV ELISA was negative
Sputum induction was non-diagnostic
BAL fluid was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii on Grocott’s methenamine silver stain
Treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and a prednisone taper with clinical and radiographic resolution of infiltrates after 2 weeks
Developed leukopenia after discontinuation of TMP-SMX
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with evidence of cardiac dysfunction and conduction abnormalities
salient_findings: Recurrent syncope over 24 hours
New left bundle branch block on ECG
Moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
Prolonged QTc interval on ECG
Intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats on telemetry
key_facts: 50-year-old man with a remote history of treated Lyme disease
No hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or diabetes
Four episodes of syncope over 24 hours
Initial workup six weeks earlier was unrevealing
New left bundle branch block on outpatient ECG
Exercise stress testing provoked presyncope with a brief burst of atrial tachycardia
LVEF of 42% with a moderate-size area of inferior wall ischaemia and scar on pharmacological nuclear stress test
No chest pain or heart failure symptoms
Vital signs: blood pressure 140/66 mmHg, heart rate 54 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.2°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Physical examination was unremarkable
12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm at 57 bpm, first-degree AV block, and a prolonged QTc
Brief burst of atrial tachycardia that resolved with IV metoprolol
Cardiac enzymes, thyroid function tests, serum calcium, and ACE levels were normal
Lyme antibody testing was negative
Chest radiograph was normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed an LVEF of 45–50% with no regional wall motion abnormalities
Telemetry captured intermittent high-grade AV block with ventricular escape beats
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography showed an LVEF of 35–40%
Permanent dual-chamber pacemaker was implanted
Outpatient cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an LVEF of 31%, RV ejection fraction of 23%, and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal anteroseptal wall
Contrast-enhanced CT scan of the chest showed mediastinal and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
